item.title: Report: IDF to replace Border Police in Judea and Samaria, freeing officers to combat crime
item.description: Senior officials from the IDF, Israel Security Agency (Shin Bet), and Israel Police met and decided that IDF soldiers would take over some of the duties currently performed by Border Police officers in Judea and Samaria, allowing the officers to focus on combating nationalist crime and riots in the area, Kan 11 News reported.

item.title: Hegseth confirms secret Israel visit, declines to discuss Netanyahu meeting
item.description: US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth confirms an unannounced visit to Israel and meeting with Netanyahu, but declines to reveal what was discussed.

item.title: Major twist in Highway 1 terror plot: Informant admits he lied
item.description: The man whose report led to the arrests on Highway 1 has been located and admitted that he lied. The suspects are apparently not terrorists, but the Shin Bet investigation is ongoing.

item.title: "Sign of life" from Kim Jong Un
item.description: North Korea has released new photographs of Kim Jong Un and his 13-year-old daughter following rumors that the dictator died of a brain hemorrhage.

item.title: Kedumim: 9-year-old spots suspicious object in Samaria, prevents disaster
item.description: A 9-year-old boy from Kedumim spotted a suspicious object near the community and alerted his father. Security forces discovered it was a missile fuel tank left from the war with Iran and safely removed it.

item.title: A week to the elections: Netanyahu leads by 10 seats, five parties don't qualify
item.description: One week before the elections, Channel 14 poll: Likud leads with 30 seats, Amcha Yisrael falls far below threshold.

item.description: France will deploy military forces in Paris and Marseille, Italy will station 500 soldiers in Milan, and Albania reports 295 people injured.

item.title: Nahal commander honors fallen comrades and inspires a new generation of IDF soldiers
item.description: After fighting on October 7, taking part in battles across the Gaza Strip and losing his comrades in Rafah, Captain Y. looks to the new generation of recruits with great faith, 'the spirit of victory of the Jewish people is stronger than ever.'

item.title: IDF eliminates senior Hamas security official in Gaza City
item.description: The IDF and Shin Bet eliminated Akram Bassam Shaaban Yassin, a senior Hamas official responsible for protecting the terrorist organization's leadership.

item.description: Fifteen cadets graduate as Hashmonaim Brigade’s first officers. Chief of staff says they are breaking new ground in integrating haredim into the IDF and building the brigade’s command echelon.

item.description: In a first-ever interview with Abu Ali Express, the Religious Zionism leader calls to dismantle the Palestinian Authority, pledges an ambitious expansion of Jewish communities, and promises further tax cuts.

item.description: The IDF and Shin Bet eliminated a Hamas terrorist who participated in the abduction of Shani Louk during the October 7 massacre.

item.title: $6 billion deal? New proposal aims to open Iran’s nuclear sites to inspectors
item.description:
A new mediation proposal reportedly calls for the release of $6 billion in frozen Iranian funds in exchange for Iran allowing International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) inspectors to visit its nuclear sites.
According to the Qatari-based Al-Araby Al-Jadeed news outlet, Qatar and Pakistan are behind the proposal, which would release $6 billion in interest accrued on Iranian funds frozen in Qatari banks in return for a covert visit by IAEA inspectors to Iran’s nuclear facilities.
The report says the proposal has received US approval and preliminary Iranian agreement. However, no official confirmation of an agreement has been issued.

item.title: Pressure mounts on Winter: Netanyahu and Smotrich meet with Rabbi Sadan
item.description: The Prime Minister and Finance Minister are currently meeting with Rabbi Eli Sadan, Ofer Winter's rabbi, amid efforts to persuade him to withdraw from the election race.

item.title: First in Israel: New brain pacemaker treats epilepsy without opening the skull
item.description: A groundbreaking medical device that stimulates the brain without opening the skull offers new hope to epilepsy patients who cannot be helped by medication or conventional surgery.

item.title: Herzog in Hungary: 'Alliance of freedom-loving nations critical to confronting Iran'
item.description: President Isaac Herzog met Hungarian President András Baka in Budapest, praising Hungary's commitment to combating antisemitism and strengthening ties with Israel.

item.title: High alert: The Chief of Staff's pre-election message
item.description: IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir visited a large-scale Gaza Division exercise and warned that Israel's enemies continue planning attacks despite suffering heavy blows.

item.title: French riots: Messi memorabilia looted
item.description: A Barcelona match jersey and captain's armband bearing the Argentine star's signature were stolen from a store in central Paris during the riots in the French capital.

item.title: Walla! poll: Hendel in, Winter out. Eisenkot's lead grows

item.title: IDF develops new test that could change who gets recruited
item.description: The IDF is developing a new assessment to uncover hidden talents and open military career paths to candidates who may have been overlooked by traditional recruitment screening.
